candidates.name: Turn of the month, US equity index futures
candidates.exact_rule: T = last NYSE session of month, T+j = j-th session of next month (planned NYSE calendar). Base: long ES (ES16 from futures_1600, F_ES as timing check) over return days T-1..T+3 (enter close T-2, exit close T+3), flat (T-bill) otherwise. Size L = min(5, 0.10/(sigma*sqrt(f))) fixed per window, sigma = sqrt(252*EWMA_com60(r^2)) of ES daily excess returns through the decision date, f = share of trailing 252 sessions inside the rule's windows. Engine exec=next_close with decision dated two sessions before the first return day (calendar known in advance). V1: return days T..T+3 (exact Lakonishok-Smidt / McConnell-Xu window). V2: same base window on an equal-risk basket of SPY, EFA, EEM, VGK, EWJ (McConnell-Xu international evidence) at ETF config costs. Costs ES 1 bp one-way (2x stress).
candidates.instruments: ES (ES16 / F_ES); V2: SPY EFA EEM VGK EWJ
candidates.data_needed: futures_1600 ES16 or futures_daily F_ES, rf_daily, NYSE calendar (edges/calendar/calcommon.py nyse_calendar), etf_daily for V2
candidates.external_evidence: Lakonishok-Smidt: DJIA 1897-1986, last day + first 3 days carry most of the return. McConnell-Xu (2008): CRSP 1926-2005, the whole market excess return accrues on days -1..+3 and the effect persists after the 1988 publication and in 30 of 35 countries. Etula et al. (2020): CRSP VW 1995-2013 holding return +77 bp/month over T-3..T+3. Counter: Maberly-Waggoner (2000) find TOM gone in S&P futures after 1990; later studies report weakening after ~2001 and concentration on day +1 in the ETF era.
candidates.adaptation_note: Base is identical to the parallel edge-search series edges/series/CAL_TOM_ES.parquet (ES16, T-1..T+3, same sizing), not yet verifier-confirmed; reuse it once its verdict is in rather than recomputing.

candidates.name: Dash for cash: settlement-adjusted month-end reversal
candidates.exact_rule: Let S = last session whose equity trades settle by month-end T: S = T-4 while US equity settlement is T+3 (through 2017-09-04), S = T-3 under T+2 (2017-09-05 to 2024-05-27), S = T-2 under T+1 (from 2024-05-28). Base: long ES over return days S+1..T+3 (enter close S, exit close T+3), flat otherwise; L = min(5, 0.10/(sigma*sqrt(f))) as in the TOM rule, decision two sessions before the first return day, exec=next_close. V1: fixed paper window, long over T-3..T+3 regardless of settlement regime. V2: base plus a short leg over return days T-8..S (institutional selling-pressure window) at the same L (time-series long-short). Costs ES 1 bp one-way.
candidates.data_needed: futures_1600 ES16 / F_ES, rf_daily, NYSE planned calendar, settlement-cycle change dates (SEC: 2017-09-05 T+2, 2024-05-28 T+1)
candidates.external_evidence: US 1995-2013 (after the 1995 T+3 rule): CRSP VW holding return -17 bp over T-8..T-4 and +77 bp over T-3..T+3; abnormal -37 bp vs +48 bp per month. 22 other markets: T-8..T-4 vs T-3..T-1 returns negatively correlated in all 23 markets, significant in 20; a settlement-rule change serves as a quasi-experiment. ANcerno 1999-2013: institutions net sellers peaking on T-4. 2014+ and the 2017 and 2024 settlement shifts are genuine out-of-sample tests of the mechanism.
candidates.adaptation_note: Index futures instead of CRSP cash index; the settlement-day shift is the paper's own mechanism applied point-in-time (rule changes were announced months ahead). Overlaps the TOM candidate on T..T+3; report correlation with it.

candidates.name: Treasury month-end index-extension across the curve
sources: Hartley & Schwarz 2019, Predictable End-of-Month Treasury Returns, Rodney White Center WP 17-19
candidates.exact_rule: Base: long an equal-risk basket of F_ZF, F_ZN, F_ZB, F_UB over return days T-2..T (enter close T-3, exit close T); leg weights proportional to 1/sigma_i (EWMA com60), basket scaled with L = min(5, 0.10/(sigma_basket*sqrt(f))), sigma_basket from the trailing 252-day covariance; decision two sessions before first return day, exec=next_close. V1: ZN only (identical to edges CAL_TSY_ME_ZN base). V2: basket over return days T-1..T. Costs ZF 0.7, ZN 1, ZB/UB 1.5 bp one-way; roll days charged by the engine.
candidates.data_needed: futures_daily F_ZF F_ZN F_ZB F_UB (or ZN16), rf_daily, NYSE calendar
candidates.external_evidence: Treasury data 1990-2018: excess returns positive and highly significant only in the last few days of the month (about 20-25 bp/month at the 10-year), a last-days long gives an annualised Sharpe of about 1 across maturities; spills over into Treasury futures and swaps; life insurers net buyers on index rebalancing dates. Post-paper (2019+) evidence: our own F1/F2 sleeves include this window and their later-window ensemble Sharpe was about -0.1 (descriptive).
candidates.adaptation_note: V1 equals edges/series/CAL_TSY_ME_ZN.parquet (unverified at time of writing). The curve basket is the new part; UB starts 2010 in our data.

candidates.name: Pre-holiday premium in small caps
sources: Ko & Yang 2021 Critical Finance Review replication
candidates.exact_rule: H = each scheduled NYSE full-day holiday (standard holiday list, unscheduled closures excluded; edges/calendar/calcommon.py pre_holiday_mask). Base: long F_RTY over the return day H-1 (last session before the holiday; enter close H-2, exit close H-1), flat otherwise; L = min(5, 0.10/(sigma*sqrt(f))) with sigma from RTY, decision two sessions ahead, exec=next_close. V1: same on ES (Ariel's large-cap index; identical to edges CAL_PREHOL_ES). V2: RTY over return days H-2..H-1. Costs RTY 2 bp, ES 1 bp one-way.
candidates.data_needed: futures_daily F_RTY, F_ES/ES16, rf_daily, NYSE holiday calendar
candidates.external_evidence: Ariel (1990): CRSP 1963-1982 pre-holiday returns 9-14 times ordinary days. Ko & Yang (2021, CFR replication, 1983-2019): out of sample the premium survives only in small firms; large-firm pre-holiday vs other-day differences insignificant, especially after 1990. Earlier: Vergin & McGinnis (1999) find it gone for large caps 1987-1996.
candidates.adaptation_note: Base switched to RTY because the out-of-sample replication says only small caps retain the effect; about 9 trading days a year, so a long-only low-exposure sleeve.

candidates.name: Pre-FOMC announcement drift (intraday ES)
candidates.exact_rule: Scheduled FOMC statement days from edges/calendar/fomc_scheduled.csv (day0; unscheduled meetings excluded). Hourly ES.v.0 bars (UTC bar start, convert to America/New_York). Base: long ES from the close of the bar starting 13:00 ET on the session before day0 to the close of the bar starting 13:00 ET on day0 (the 14:00-to-14:00 window, statement at 14:00/14:15); for the 2011-04..2012-12 press-conference meetings with 12:30 statements use the bar starting 11:00 ET on both days. Event return booked on day0; daily series sized L = min(5, 0.10/(sigma*sqrt(f))), sigma = ES daily EWMA vol, f = 8/252 events. V1: overnight-only window, from the 16:00 ET close of the session before day0 to the close of the bar starting 08:00 ET on day0 (post-2011 drift migrated overnight per Knox & Vissing-Jorgensen). V2: daily version on ES16, long return day0 only (close d-1 to close d). Costs ES 1 bp per side, one round trip per event.
candidates.data_needed: databento_raw/glbx_ohlcv1h_v01_es_zn.parquet (ES.v.0, 2010-06+), FOMC scheduled dates CSV, futures_1600 ES16 for V2
candidates.external_evidence: Lucca-Moench: Sep 1994-Mar 2011 S&P 500 rose 49 bp on average in the 24h before scheduled statements, about 80% of the realised equity premium; no reversal. Kurov-Wolfe-Gilbert: the drift essentially disappeared after 2015 (sample to Dec 2019), with and without press conferences. Knox & Vissing-Jorgensen (2026 survey): Apr 2011-Dec 2023 still about 20 bp average return overnight before the announcement; Boguth et al. (2019): 2011-2017 premium only for press-conference meetings; options-implied FOMC-day premium only 1-2 bp.
candidates.adaptation_note: Hourly bars force 14:00 instead of 14:15 exits (always pre-announcement); hourly data start 2010-06, so the IS window is entirely post-Lucca-Moench sample, a genuine out-of-sample test.

candidates.name: FOMC cycle even weeks
candidates.exact_rule: Cycle day k = sessions since the most recent scheduled FOMC statement day (k=0 on day0, k=-1 the session before). Long ES on return days with k in {-1..3, 9..13, 19..23, 29..33}, flat otherwise; L = min(5, 0.10/(sigma*sqrt(f))), decision two sessions ahead, exec=next_close. No variants (identical to edges CAL_FOMC_EVEN_ES). Cost ES 1 bp.
candidates.data_needed: ES16/F_ES, FOMC scheduled CSV, NYSE calendar
candidates.external_evidence: CMVJ: 1994-2016 the entire US equity premium earned in even FOMC-cycle weeks (0,2,4,6), holds in 2014-2016 and internationally. Knox & Vissing-Jorgensen (2026): 2017-2021 a statistically significant opposite cycle; even-week effect 8.2 bp/day over 1994-2023 per Nagel & Xu (2024), mostly from yield declines. Post-publication failure is documented.
candidates.adaptation_note: Already computed by the parallel edge search (edges/series/CAL_FOMC_EVEN_ES.parquet, unverified); listed for completeness, do not recompute.

candidates.name: FOMC announcement reversal (intraday ES)
sources: Baglioni & Ribeiro 2022 WP 'The FOMC announcement reversal'
candidates.exact_rule: Hourly ES.v.0. On each scheduled statement day0, r_pre = close of bar starting 13:00 ET on day0 / close of bar starting 13:00 ET on the previous session - 1 (use 11:00 ET bars for the 2011-04..2012-12 12:30 statements). Position = -sign(r_pre) from the close of the bar starting 13:00 ET (or 11:00) to the close of the bar starting 15:00 ET on day0 (16:00 ET). Size per event: notional = 0.10/(sigma_win*sqrt(8/252)) capped at 5, sigma_win = trailing 252-session EWMA vol of the same 14:00-16:00 window on all days, annualised. V1: trade only when |r_pre| > 0.5 x trailing sd of 24h pre-windows. V2: same rule on ZN.v.0 (exit 15:00 ET). Costs ES 1 bp, ZN 1.5 bp per side.
candidates.data_needed: glbx_ohlcv1h_v01_es_zn.parquet, FOMC scheduled CSV
candidates.external_evidence: Baglioni-Ribeiro: E-mini, Oct 1997-Jan 2020 (180 scheduled meetings, subperiods 1997-2011 and 2011-2020): pre-announcement and post-announcement returns negatively related; the reversal strategy's Sharpe about 2.5x that of the pre-FOMC drift. Single working paper, no independent replication found.
candidates.adaptation_note: Paper enters at 13:50; hourly bars give the 14:00 boundary (last trade before the statement). Only 8 events a year, so the annual-scale Sharpe will be noisy.

candidates.name: Macro announcement-day equity premium
candidates.exact_rule: A-days = union of scheduled BLS Employment Situation release dates, CPI release dates, PPI release dates (all 08:30 ET) and scheduled FOMC statement days. Base: long ES over return day d for each A-day d (enter close d-1, exit close d), flat otherwise; L = min(5, 0.10/(sigma*sqrt(f))), f = trailing share of A-days, decision two sessions ahead (dates published a year in advance), exec=next_close. V1: Savor-Wilson set exactly (PPI + Employment + FOMC). V2: Employment + FOMC only. Cost ES 1 bp.
candidates.data_needed: ES16/F_ES; release dates scraped from BLS archive pages bls.gov/bls/news-release/empsit.htm, cpi.htm, ppi.htm (free); FOMC scheduled CSV
candidates.external_evidence: Savor-Wilson: 1958-2009 excess return 11.4 bp on announcement days vs 1.1 bp otherwise, over 60% of the annual premium on ~13% of days, Sharpe about 10x; holds in 9 of 10 five-year subsamples. Ernst-Gilbert-Hrdlicka (2021): after removing sample selection and day-of-month timing effects, announcement days carry about half of the premium with Sharpe similar to other days. Samadi (2024): long-history FOMC (since 1936) 12 bp and NFP (since 1928) 8 bp average.
candidates.adaptation_note: About 30-36 A-days a year; overlaps the TOM window via first-Friday payroll releases, report the TOM-excluded variant as a diagnostic only (not a declared variant).

candidates.name: Macro announcement-day Treasury premium
candidates.exact_rule: A-days as in calendar_event_macro_announcement_es (Employment, CPI, PPI, scheduled FOMC). Base: long equal-risk F_ZN + F_ZB over return day d of each A-day, flat otherwise; legs 1/sigma_i weighted, L = min(5, 0.10/(sigma_basket*sqrt(f))), decision two sessions ahead, exec=next_close. V1: ZN only. V2: Employment + PPI days only (Jones-Lamont-Lumsdaine set). Costs ZN 1, ZB 1.5 bp.
candidates.data_needed: futures_daily F_ZN F_ZB, BLS release-date archives, FOMC CSV
candidates.external_evidence: Jones-Lamont-Lumsdaine: 1979-1993 large bond risk premium on employment/PPI release days, zero excess return over bills on other days, no volatility persistence. Savor-Wilson: 1961-2009 Treasury announcement-day premium rises monotonically with maturity, Sharpe much higher on announcement days. No post-2009 test found.
candidates.adaptation_note: Futures (CTD-based) instead of CRSP constant-maturity bonds. 2022 hiking cycle will be a stress test.

candidates.name: Announcement-day beta premium (sector ETFs)
sources: Savor & Wilson 2014 JFE 'Asset pricing: a tale of two days'
candidates.exact_rule: Universe: XLB XLE XLF XLI XLK XLP XLU XLV XLY. At each close compute trailing 252-session beta of each ETF to SPY (daily excess returns through the decision date). Base: on A-days (as in the macro-announcement candidate) hold long the 3 highest-beta and short the 3 lowest-beta sectors, legs equal-weighted and scaled so the book's ex-ante beta to SPY is 0, flat on other days; book scaled to 10% ex-ante vol with L = min(5, 0.10/(sigma*sqrt(f))), sigma from trailing returns of the A-day book applied daily. V1: also hold the reversed book (long low-beta / short high-beta) on non-announcement days. V2: same on the 30 futures ranked by beta to ES (ex-ante beta-neutral). ETF costs config.cost_bps + 30 bp/yr borrow on shorts; futures per task table.
candidates.instruments: 9 SPDR sector ETFs, SPY; V2 30 futures
candidates.data_needed: etf_daily (1998+), BLS release dates, FOMC CSV, futures_daily for V2
candidates.external_evidence: Savor-Wilson (2014): 1964-2011 the SML slope is 6.81 bp per unit beta on announcement days and zero or negative on other days, for stocks, test portfolios, bonds and currencies. Related: Hendershott, Livdan & Rosch (2020 JFE) beta priced overnight not intraday; Wachter & Zhu (2022 RFS) model. No net-of-cost tradable replication on ETFs found.
candidates.adaptation_note: Sector ETFs replace beta-sorted stock portfolios; beta dispersion across sectors is narrower, so expect a smaller spread.

candidates.name: FOMC-day short-dollar premium
candidates.exact_rule: Base: on each scheduled FOMC statement day0 hold an equal-risk long basket of F_6E F_6J F_6B F_6A F_6C F_6S (short USD) over return day0 (F_* closes are end of the UTC day, so day0 includes the 14:00 ET statement); legs 1/sigma_i, L = min(5, 0.10/(sigma_basket*sqrt(8/252))), decision two sessions ahead, exec=next_close; flat otherwise. V1: only the 3 currencies with the highest trailing carry (annualised log ratio of second to front contract price from glbx_ohlcv1d .v.0/.v.1, sign so that positive = higher foreign rate). V2: hold return days -1 and 0. Costs FX futures 1 bp.
candidates.data_needed: futures_daily FX roots; glbx_ohlcv1d_v01.parquet front/second closes for V1 carry; FOMC CSV
candidates.external_evidence: MTV: tick data 1994-2013, 10 currencies: short-USD basket earns 17.28 bp on FOMC days vs 1.16 bp other days (t 2.51); high-rate portfolio 14.47 vs 1.73 bp, low-rate 5.19 vs -0.51 bp; returns larger with monetary-policy uncertainty and during easing; announcement-day Sharpe up to 0.8 after costs (1998-2013 forwards). 2014+ is out of sample and untested in published work we found.
candidates.adaptation_note: Futures replace forwards; the dollar index of the paper is replaced by our 6 G10 futures (no NZD, SEK, NOK).

candidates.name: Treasury duration in 3-day FOMC windows
sources: Hillenbrand 2025 RFS 'The Fed and the Secular Decline in Interest Rates'
candidates.exact_rule: Base: long F_ZN over return days -1, 0, +1 around each scheduled FOMC statement day0 (enter close of day -2, exit close of day +1), flat otherwise; L = min(5, 0.10/(sigma*sqrt(f))), f = trailing share of window days (~24/252), decision two sessions ahead, exec=next_close. V1: F_ZB instead. V2: equal-risk F_ZF/F_ZN/F_ZB/F_UB basket. Costs ZN 1, ZB/UB 1.5, ZF 0.7 bp.
candidates.instruments: ZN (V1 ZB; V2 ZF ZN ZB UB)
candidates.data_needed: futures_daily rates roots, FOMC CSV
candidates.external_evidence: Hillenbrand: 1980/1989-2019 essentially the entire secular decline in long-term Treasury yields (about 8 pp in the 10-year 1980-2017) occurred in 3-day windows around FOMC meetings; yield moves outside the windows are transitory; driven by rate cuts and lower dot-plot long-run rates. Knox & Vissing-Jorgensen (2026) report 30-year yields falling over 3-day FOMC windows in both 1994-2011 and 2011-2023. The 2022 hiking cycle is the obvious risk.
candidates.adaptation_note: Futures instead of zero-coupon yields; the source is a yield-change decomposition, not a backtest net of costs.

candidates.name: FOMC premium in non-US equities
sources: Brusa, Savor & Wilson 2020 Review of Finance 24(2)
candidates.exact_rule: Base: long an equal-risk basket of EFA, EEM, VGK, EWJ (US-listed, 16:00 ET closes, so return day0 contains the 14:00 statement) over return days -1 and 0 of each scheduled FOMC statement; legs 1/sigma_i, L = min(5, 0.10/(sigma_basket*sqrt(f))), decision two sessions ahead, exec=next_close; flat otherwise. V1: day 0 only. V2: add SPY to the basket. ETF costs config.cost_bps.
candidates.data_needed: etf_daily, FOMC CSV
candidates.external_evidence: Brusa-Savor-Wilson: 1998-2016, global stock markets earn high returns on days around FOMC meetings, but not around ECB, BoE, BoJ or eight other central banks (not driven by surprises or FX moves). Lucca-Moench and CMVJ also report the pre-FOMC / cycle effect in international indices. Post-2016 untested in published work found.
candidates.adaptation_note: Local indices close before 14:00 ET, so US-listed ETFs are used; their day-0 return mixes local-close and US-afternoon information.

candidates.name: Treasury auction cycle (2-year note butterfly)
sources: Lou, Yan & Zhang 2013 RFS 'Anticipated and repeated shocks in liquid markets'
candidates.exact_rule: Auction dates A from treasury_auctions.parquet: security_type Note, original_security_term 2-Year, auction_date mapped to the NYSE session. Hedge ratio beta = trailing 60-session OLS slope of F_ZT daily returns on F_ZN returns (data through the decision date). Base: over return days A-9..A (enter close A-10, exit close A) hold short 1 ZT + long beta ZN (duration-neutral; the paper's 6-month bill leg is cash); over return days A+1..A+10 hold the reverse; overlapping windows net. Spread scaled to 10% ex-ante vol with sigma = EWMA com60 of the spread's daily returns; decision two sessions ahead (auction dates announced about a week ahead, calendar regular), exec=next_close. V1: 5-year auctions, short ZF vs long duration-matched ZT+ZN pair before, reverse after. V2: base with 5-session windows (A-4..A and A+1..A+5). Costs ZT 0.5, ZF 0.7, ZN 1 bp.
candidates.data_needed: futures_daily F_ZT F_ZF F_ZN, treasury_auctions.parquet (2002-2026), NYSE calendar
candidates.external_evidence: LYZ: 1980-2008 secondary prices fall in the days before auctions and recover after; 2-year strategy (short 2y vs duration-matched 6m bill + 10y for 10 days before, reverse 10 days after) earns 8.62 bp per cycle (t 3.65), Sharpe 1.08 full sample, 1.44 in 1998-2008, about 0.95 after bid-ask; 5-year note 5-day pre/post differential 22.5 bp (t 3.67). Independent: Sigaux (2023 JBF, Italian auctions, mechanism), Beetsma et al. (euro area), TIPS auction cycle (EFMA 2020: inflation swaps -3.35 bp pre-auction). Post-2008 US futures evidence not found.
candidates.adaptation_note: Futures butterflies instead of on-the-run cash notes; ZT tracks the 2-year sector only roughly (CTD). Monthly 2-year auctions make the windows cover most days.

candidates.name: Option-expiration week
candidates.exact_rule: X = standard monthly equity-option expiration = third Friday of the month (the preceding session if that Friday is an exchange holiday). Base: long ES over the return days of the expiration week, Monday..X (enter close of the last session before that week, exit close X), flat otherwise; L = min(5, 0.10/(sigma*sqrt(f))), decision two sessions ahead, exec=next_close. V1: Monday..Thursday before X (excludes expiration day, which practitioner tests find negative). V2: base only in March, June, September, December (quarterly expirations). Cost ES 1 bp.
candidates.data_needed: ES16/F_ES, rf_daily, NYSE calendar
candidates.external_evidence: Stivers-Sun: S&P 500 1983-2008 option-expiration-week returns unusually high (not before 1983); 28 optioned large caps 1996-2008 0.45%/week vs 0.12% other weeks, weekly Sharpe 0.57 vs 0.07; week after expiration -0.03%. Practitioner SPY test 1993-2025: about 2% CAGR at about 20% time invested, deteriorated over the last four years.
candidates.adaptation_note: Weekly and 0DTE options since 2016-2022 dilute the monthly expiration channel; expect decay.

candidates.name: Halloween / sell in May
sources: Jacobsen & Zhang (Halloween indicator everywhere and all the time)
candidates.exact_rule: Base: long ES over return days from the first session of November to the last session of April (enter close of last October session, exit close of last April session), flat (T-bill) May-October; L = min(5, 0.10/(sigma*sqrt(f))) fixed per half-year window, f = trailing share of in-season days (~0.5), decision two sessions ahead, exec=next_close. V1: base plus long F_ZN at the same ex-ante risk during May-October (switch to bonds). V2: equal-risk basket of ES plus EFA, EEM, VGK, EWJ in the November-April window (international version). Costs ES 1 bp, ZN 1 bp, ETFs config.
candidates.instruments: ES (V1 ZN; V2 EFA EEM VGK EWJ)
candidates.data_needed: ES16/F_ES, F_ZN, etf_daily, rf_daily
candidates.external_evidence: Andrade-Chhaochharia-Fuerst out-of-sample test on Bouman-Jacobsen's 37 markets, Nov 1998-Apr 2012: Nov-Apr returns about 10 pp higher than May-Oct; a half-exposure timing rule Sharpe 0.52 vs 0.17 buy-and-hold. Jacobsen & Zhang: 108 markets 1693-2011, winter minus summer 4.52% (t 9.69), 6.25% over the last 50 years, present in 81 of 108 markets. Counter: Dichtl & Drobetz (2015) find no net benefit in recent data after costs.
candidates.adaptation_note: Index futures replace cash indices; only about 14 winters in-sample, so the Newey-West t will be weak even if the effect is real; the long-history evidence carries the case.

candidates.name: Turn-of-the-year small-cap spread
sources: Moller & Zilca 2008 JBF 'The evolution of the January effect'
candidates.exact_rule: Base: long F_RTY / short F_ES with ES notional = trailing 252-session beta of RTY on ES (ex-ante beta-neutral) over return days from the first session after December 15 through the 5th session of January (enter close of the last session on or before Dec 15, exit close of the 5th January session); spread scaled with L = min(5, 0.10/(sigma_spread*sqrt(f))), decision two sessions ahead, exec=next_close. V1: window = first 10 sessions of January (Moller-Zilca first-half January). V2: long RTY outright over the base window. Costs RTY 2, ES 1 bp.
candidates.data_needed: futures_daily F_RTY F_ES, rf_daily
candidates.external_evidence: Keim (1983) and successors: small firms earn abnormal returns in early January. Moller-Zilca (2008): daily size-decile evidence shows the effect shortened and concentrated in the first half of January, with mean reversion in the second half. Practitioner data: since 1990 January small-cap returns modest (Russell 2000 Jan avg 1.4%, 55% win rate since 1979) and the effect has migrated into late December.
candidates.adaptation_note: RTY futures (Russell 2000) proxy the small-firm portfolio; only about 14 events in-sample.

candidates.name: Same-calendar-month seasonality, cross-section of futures
candidates.exact_rule: Monthly, at the last session of month m-1 (decision), for each futures root compute the average monthly excess return (F_* total-return index minus rf) in calendar month m over the previous up-to-10 years (at least 5 observations). Base (commodities, Baltas spec): rank the 15 commodities CL HO RB NG GC SI PL HG ZC ZS ZW ZL ZM LE HE, long top 3 / short bottom 3, legs 1/sigma_i (EWMA com60), book scaled to 10% ex-ante vol with the trailing 252-day covariance, held through month m (exec next_close). V1: same on all 30 futures, top/bottom 6. V2: time-series version per commodity, sign of its same-month average, equal-risk, 10% target. Costs per task table (grains/livestock 4 bp, NG/HO/RB/PL 3, CL/GC/SI/HG 2).
candidates.data_needed: futures_daily (2010-06+); with the 5-year minimum the first signal is mid-2015 (IS about 2015-06..2024-10). Optional history extension for signal estimation only: free yfinance continuous front-month (CL=F etc.) back to 2000, accepting roll-gap noise.
candidates.external_evidence: KLN (2016): same-calendar-month seasonalities in stocks (13%/yr), anomalies, commodities and country indices. Baltas (2016): commodities since 1992, 10-year same-month quintile long-short about 4% gross per year, gross Sharpe 0.49, but high turnover makes it hard to capture net. Out-of-sample 2016-2024 (arXiv 2609.12227, 15 commodities, rolling 10-year windows, costs included): no seasonal model beats the equal-weight benchmark after Holm adjustment.
candidates.adaptation_note: Short history is the binding constraint; this candidate also stands in for practitioner single-commodity seasonals (natural gas, gasoline, livestock), which are spot-price seasonals largely priced into futures curves.

candidates.name: Same-calendar-month seasonality, sector and country ETFs
candidates.exact_rule: Universe base: 9 SPDR sectors XLB XLE XLF XLI XLK XLP XLU XLV XLY. At the last session of month m-1 compute each ETF's average monthly excess return in calendar month m over the previous up-to-10 years (minimum 5); long top 3 / short bottom 3, legs 1/sigma_i, book 10% ex-ante vol from the trailing 252-day covariance, held through month m, exec next_close. V1 (front-running, per Quantpedia): rank on calendar month m+1 instead of m. V2: universe = 9 sectors + SPY EFA EEM VGK EWJ (14). ETF costs config.cost_bps + 30 bp/yr borrow on shorts.
candidates.instruments: 9 sector SPDRs (V2 + SPY EFA EEM VGK EWJ)
candidates.data_needed: etf_daily (sectors from 1998-12; first signal 2003-12 with the 5-year minimum), rf_daily
candidates.external_evidence: Heston-Sadka: stocks that outperform in a calendar month keep outperforming in the same month for up to 5+ years; internationally (Canada, Japan, 12 European markets) global seasonal strategies beat non-seasonal ones by over 1%/month, robust to size/value/beta. KLN extend to country indices and industries. Quantpedia front-running backtests on sector and country ETFs through Feb 2025 report Sharpe about 1.1 (likely optimistic, not peer reviewed).
candidates.adaptation_note: Only 9-14 assets, so ranking noise is large; sector-level seasonality is weaker than stock-level in the literature.

candidates.name: Seasonality-filtered trend following
sources: Baltas 2016 Bankers Markets & Investors 140 'Multi-asset seasonality and trend-following strategies'
candidates.exact_rule: Base trend book: 12-month TSMOM sign on each of the 30 futures (sign of trailing 252-session excess return), equal-risk 1/sigma_i, book scaled to 10% ex-ante vol, rebalanced monthly at the last session (exec next_close). Overlay: for the coming month m set an asset's position to zero when the sign of its same-calendar-month average excess return over the prior up-to-10 years (minimum 5) disagrees with its trend sign. Report the overlay minus base difference too. V1: halve instead of zero. V2: commodities only (15). Costs per task table.
candidates.data_needed: futures_daily (seasonal signals from mid-2015 with the 5-year minimum), rf_daily
candidates.external_evidence: Baltas (2016): switching off trend positions that disagree with same-month seasonality significantly improves raw trend following in commodities and equity indices; the improvement survives realistic futures costs with position smoothing. No later independent replication found.
candidates.adaptation_note: Directly usable for Workflow 2 as an add-on to the existing TSMOM leg (our TSMOM 12-month on 20 futures: 0.28 IS).

candidates.name: Overnight drift at the European open (buy the dip)
sources: Boyarchenko, Larsen & Whelan 2023 RFS 36(9) 'The overnight drift'
Cliff, Cooper & Gulen 2008 'Return differences between trading and non-trading hours'
candidates.exact_rule: Hourly ES.v.0 bars converted to America/New_York. Base (buy-the-dip, BtD): if the ES return from the 16:00 ET close of session d-1 to the 16:00 ET close of session d is negative (proxy for the paper's negative closing order flow), go long ES from the open of the bar starting 01:00 ET to the close of the bar starting 03:00 ET of the following night (01:00-04:00 ET, adapting the paper's 01:30-03:30); flat otherwise. Size per trade: notional = min(5, 0.10/(sigma_w*sqrt(f))), sigma_w = annualised EWMA (com 60) vol of the 01:00-04:00 window returns, f = trailing share of trading nights. V1: unconditional, bar starting 02:00 ET only (02:00-03:00, the paper's OD), every night. V2: unconditional close-to-open, 16:00 ET close to close of the bar starting 08:00 ET (night effect). Costs ES 1 bp per side (2 bp per round trip, report 2x).
candidates.data_needed: glbx_ohlcv1h_v01_es_zn.parquet (ES.v.0, check overnight bar coverage, roll handling via instrument_id)
candidates.external_evidence: BLW: 1998-2020, ES returns between 02:00 and 03:00 ET average 3.7%/yr (1.48 bp/day), positive in 20 of 23 years; 2004-2020: OD Sharpe 1.1 gross but -0.5 after bid-ask; OD+ (01:30-03:30) 1.3 gross, 0.3 net; buy-the-dip after negative closing order flow Sharpe 1.8 gross, in the market ~50% of days. NY Fed blog: full overnight session 2.6%/yr of a 4.3%/yr close-to-close return (1998-2019). Cliff-Cooper-Gulen: 1993-2006 overnight returns positive, daytime about zero.
candidates.adaptation_note: At 1 bp per side the round trip (2 bp) is larger than the unconditional nightly mean (about 1.5 bp), so only the conditional base has a chance net; the actual ES spread (0.25 pt, about 0.5 bp) is below our cost assumption, report gross too.

candidates.name: Market intraday momentum (last hour)
sources: Gao, Han, Li & Zhou 2018 JFE 'Market intraday momentum'
candidates.exact_rule: Hourly .v.0 bars in America/New_York. ES: r_ROD = return from the 16:00 ET close of the previous session to the close of the bar starting 14:00 ET (15:00 ET); hold sign(r_ROD) x notional over the bar starting 15:00 ET (15:00-16:00 ET). ZN: same with the 15:00 ET pit close, r_ROD from previous 15:00 ET to 14:00 ET, hold over the bar starting 14:00 ET. Notional per market = min(5, 0.10/(sigma_LH*sqrt(1))) with sigma_LH the annualised EWMA (com 60) vol of that market's last-hour returns, then the two markets equal-risk combined. V1: trade only when |r_ROD| > 1 trailing EWMA sd of r_ROD (cuts turnover). V2: ES only. Costs ES 1 bp, ZN 1.5 bp per side (intraday).
candidates.data_needed: glbx_ohlcv1h_v01_es_zn.parquet (2010-06..2026-10)
candidates.external_evidence: Gao et al.: SPY 1993-2013, first half-hour return predicts the last half-hour; timing strategy 6.67%/yr gross on SPY (11.7% IWM), 20% on FOMC-release days. Baltussen et al.: 60+ futures 1974-2020, rest-of-day return predicts the last 30 minutes in equities, bonds, commodities and FX; timing Sharpe 0.87-1.73 gross per asset class; positive net Sharpe in S&P futures at one-tick costs; stronger when option dealers are net short gamma; reverts over following days.
candidates.adaptation_note: Hourly bars give a last hour instead of the last 30 minutes (dilutes the signal) and our 1 bp per side ES cost is about two ticks, so net results hinge on V1's filter.

candidates.name: Front-running month-end 60/40 rebalancing
sources: Harvey, Mazzoleni & Melone 2025 NBER w33554 'The unintended consequences of rebalancing'
candidates.exact_rule: Track a 60/40 ES16/ZN16 portfolio reset to 60/40 at each month-end close. Calendar signal at close d inside the last 5 sessions of the month (T-4..T): s_d = w_eq,d - 0.60 with w_eq the drifted equity weight from month-to-date total returns through d; z_d = s_d / trailing 36-month sd of month-end s, capped at +-2. Base: hold -z_d units of a spread that is short ES / long ZN, each leg scaled to 10% ex-ante vol (EWMA com60), from close d+1 (exec next_close, earns return day d+2), flat outside T-3..T+1 return days; book rescaled to 10% ex-ante from the trailing spread covariance. V1: threshold signal, any day of the month, active when |w_eq - 0.60| > 0.02 (rebalancing band), same spread. V2: base only at quarter-end months. Costs ES 1, ZN 1 bp.
candidates.data_needed: futures_1600 ES16 ZN16 (or F_ES F_ZN), rf_daily
candidates.external_evidence: HMM: 1997-2023, a one-sd calendar signal predicts -17 bp next-day equity returns and +2 bp bonds; the threshold signal -16 bp / +4 bp; front-runners profit; estimated cost to funds about $16bn a year. Independent replication (Quant Returns, 2025): futures version Sharpe above 1.4, beta 0.07, skew 5.1; SPY/TLT version Sharpe 1.17. Our own F1/F2 include a month-end rebalancing-pressure sleeve; the ensemble later window was negative (descriptive).
candidates.adaptation_note: next_close execution delays the trade one day versus the paper's next-day horizon (the signal changes little day to day). Not identical to the F1 sleeve (different signal), so no reuse; report correlation with F2.

candidates.name: Month-end FX hedge rebalancing (equity-driven)
candidates.exact_rule: Local-currency equity indices: US ^GSPC (index_daily), euro area ^STOXX50E and Japan ^N225 (local_indices), UK ^FTSE, Canada ^GSPTSE, Australia ^AXJO, Switzerland ^SSMI (free yfinance). At close T-2 compute each market's return from the last close of the previous month to T-2, demean cross-sectionally across the 7 markets (USD included), giving e_c. Base: for each of 6E 6B 6J 6C 6A 6S hold weight proportional to -(e_c - e_US) (short currencies whose market outperformed), legs 1/sigma_i, normalised to 10% ex-ante vol via trailing covariance, over return day T (decision close T-2, held from close T-1, exec next_close; the 11:00 ET London 4pm fix on T lies inside). V1: hold over return days T-1..T (decision close T-3). V2: exclude 6A and 6C (commodity currencies, weak link per Chaban). Costs FX futures 1 bp.
candidates.data_needed: futures_daily FX roots, index_daily ^GSPC, local_indices ^STOXX50E ^N225, yfinance ^FTSE ^GSPTSE ^AXJO ^SSMI (free)
candidates.external_evidence: Melvin-Prins: 2004-2012, 10 developed currencies, intraday data: a country's equity outperformance over the month predicts its currency's depreciation in the hour before the end-of-month London fix (panel coefficient -0.0142, p<0.01): 10% relative equity gain gives 14 bp currency depreciation; larger at quarter and year ends. Practitioner: bank month-end FX rebalancing models are published every month.
candidates.adaptation_note: The effect sits in one hour before 11:00 ET; daily futures closes dilute it heavily (and include any post-fix reversal), so expect a weak daily signal; hourly FX data are not in the data set.

candidates.name: Front-running the GSCI (Goldman) roll
sources: Mou 2011 SSRN 1716841 'Limits to arbitrage and commodity index investment: front-running the Goldman roll'
candidates.exact_rule: Commodities CL HO RB NG GC SI HG ZC ZW ZS LE HE. S&P GSCI rolls 20% a day on business days 5-9 (BD5..BD9) of the roll month, from the current index contract to the next index contract (contract schedule from the S&P GSCI methodology). Using glbx_ohlcv1d_v01 .v.0/.v.1 closes and FREE databento symbology to identify the contract months, trade only when the roll-out contract is .v.0 and the roll-in contract is .v.1. Base: short roll-out / long roll-in (equal notional) from the close of the session 10 business days before BD5 to the close of BD4 (pure pre-roll front-running). V1: same entry, exit close BD9 (hold through the roll). V2: enter close BD4, exit close BD9 (during-roll only). Each commodity spread scaled to equal risk by trailing spread vol, book 10% ex-ante. Costs: 2x the outright one-way cost per leg per task table.
candidates.data_needed: databento_raw/glbx_ohlcv1d_v01.parquet (front and second closes, instrument_id), databento symbology.resolve (free), S&P GSCI roll schedule
candidates.external_evidence: Mou: 2000-Mar 2010, roll-period price impact statistically and economically significant; two front-running strategies give positively skewed excess returns with Sharpe up to 4.39; profits rise with index size and fall with arbitrage capital. Later evidence: roll-period abnormal price changes +115/+146 bp (nearby/deferred) before 2004 vs -60/-40 bp 2004-2010, and front-running not profitable after costs in later data.
candidates.adaptation_note: The exact entry/exit days of Mou's two strategies could not be confirmed (SSRN blocked, search budget exhausted); the three variants span the plausible definitions and must be fixed in SPEC.md from the paper before any computation.

candidates.name: Corn growing-season weather premium
sources: Janzen 2021 farmdoc daily (Univ. of Illinois): weather risk premium in new-crop corn
candidates.exact_rule: Base: short corn futures over return days from the first session of June to the last session of November (enter close of the last May session, exit close of the last November session), flat otherwise; prefer the December (new-crop) contract: from the .v.0/.v.1 daily closes pick the instrument whose symbology resolves to the current-year Z contract, else F_ZC; L = min(5, 0.10/(sigma*sqrt(f))), decision two sessions ahead, exec=next_close. V1: June 1 to September 30 only (pre-harvest). V2: the base on soybeans (F_ZS), a falsification test (the source finds no premium there). Cost grains 4 bp.
candidates.data_needed: futures_daily F_ZC F_ZS, glbx_ohlcv1d_v01 + free symbology for the Dec contract, rf_daily
candidates.external_evidence: Janzen (2021): 2000-2020, December corn futures averaged 12% higher in the first week of June than in the week of December 1, a weather premium peaking in early June; soybeans show no material premium (mid-July peak only 4% above Nov 1).
candidates.adaptation_note: Price-level comparison in the source, not a tested strategy net of costs; overlaps 2010-2020 with our in-sample window, so the IS test is not independent.

candidates.name: Mid-month payday effect
candidates.exact_rule: Base: long ES over the return day of calendar day 16 of each month (if day 16 is not a session, the next session): enter close of the previous session, exit close of that session; flat otherwise; L = min(5, 0.10/(sigma*sqrt(f))), decision two sessions ahead, exec=next_close. V1: return days of calendar days 15 and 16. V2: union of the base with the TOM window T-1..T+3. Cost ES 1 bp.
candidates.data_needed: ES16/F_ES, rf_daily
candidates.external_evidence: Ma-Pratt: 1980-2010, the 16th is the third-best calendar day, beaten only by the 1st and 2nd; Quantpedia lists holding only the 16th at 0.21%/yr return, 4.3% vol, Sharpe 0.6 (unscaled, tiny exposure). No out-of-sample test; biweekly pay schedules should erode it.
candidates.adaptation_note: About 12 days a year; mainly a diagnostic companion to the TOM / dash-for-cash candidates.

candidates.name: Russell reconstitution additions/deletions
candidates.exact_rule: Stock level: from the May rank day to the last-Friday-of-June reconstitution, long predicted Russell 2000 additions and short predicted deletions (ranked by May market cap around the 1000/3000 breakpoints), exit after reconstitution day. Requires constituent-level prices and market caps.
candidates.data_needed: stock-level prices/market caps and Russell membership (not in our data)
candidates.external_evidence: Madhavan (2003): large, predictable price pressure on additions and deletions around the June reconstitution (sample to 2002); later studies report shrinking profits as arbitrage capital grew and FTSE Russell introduced banding and announced more frequent reconstitution.
candidates.adaptation_note: No documented index-futures version (RTY vs ES around reconstitution is untested); listed for coverage only.
